summary: Reads Wacom tablet pen position, pressure, tilt, rotation, wheels, and button channels, supporting two devices on one tablet.
key_concepts: Tablet CHOP reads Wacom tablet X/Y position, pen pressure, X/Y tilt, pen buttons, wheels, and rotation channels.
The operator initializes or installs tablet support when the CHOP is created.
Two devices can be used simultaneously on the same tablet, with separate 1st Pen and 2nd Pen parameter pages.
Putting a channel name in a parameter creates that output channel; leaving the field empty suppresses the channel.
Axis channel ranges are -1.0 to 1.0, while button channels output 0 for up and 1 for down.
The Channel page controls whether values cook while off, on, or only while the timeline is playing, and sets the output sample rate.

key_params.name: xcoord
key_params.note: Channel name for pen X coordinate

key_params.name: ycoord
key_params.note: Channel name for pen Y coordinate

key_params.name: tanpressure
key_params.note: Channel name for finger wheel if available

key_params.name: zcoord
key_params.note: Channel name for thumb wheel if available

key_params.name: active
key_params.note: Off, on, or while-playing tablet capture state

key_params.name: off
key_params.note: Do not cook or update tablet values

key_params.name: on
key_params.note: Cook every frame and output pen movement

key_params.name: play
key_params.note: Capture pen events only while the timeline is playing forward

common_gotchas: Tablet CHOP initializes/installs when created and depends on Wacom tablet support.
Putting a channel name in a parameter creates that output channel; leaving it blank suppresses that channel.
Axis values are in the -1 to 1 range; button values are 0 or 1.
Supports two simultaneous devices on the same tablet, with 1st Pen and 2nd Pen pages controlling channel names.
Use channel filters or Null CHOPs downstream to stabilize names before recording or exporting.
Refer users to Wacom setup/tuning docs when sensitivity or driver setup is the real issue.
